messages.content:
You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Fennec library classes","question":"Can the coordinator report that room changes reached participants?","claims":{"A":"The workshop moved from Room 1 to Room 4.","B":"Every registered attendee received the change notice before noon.","C":"The workshop had 20 registered attendees."},"handoff":"The workshop's room change from Room 1 to Room 4 is well supported by the booking ledger (S2). The claim that every registered attendee received the change notice before noon remains unresolved: although 18 emails were sent (S3), delivery and receipt are unconfirmed, and the registration ledger (S1) shows only 18 attendees, contradicting the claim of 20. Given this, the coordinator can report the room change occurred but cannot definitively confirm that all participants received the notice.","follow_up":{}}

Claim B is contradicted because although 18 emails were sent (S3), delivery and receipt are unconfirmed, and the registration ledger (S1) shows only 18 attendees, not 20. Claim C is contradicted by the registration ledger (S1) indicating only 18 attendees, not 20. Thus, the coordinator can report the room change but cannot confirm all participants received the notice."}

parsed.note: Claim A is decisively supported by the booking ledger (S2) confirming the room change. Claim B is contradicted because although 18 emails were sent (S3), delivery and receipt are unconfirmed, and the registration ledger (S1) shows only 18 attendees, not 20. Claim C is contradicted by the registration ledger (S1) indicating only 18 attendees, not 20. Thus, the coordinator can report the room change but cannot confirm all participants received the notice.
